To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 6 Mycobacterium Massiliense smooth strains with a specific hybrid gene rpoB gene in South Korean patients.
the M. massilienese rpoB LGTs are not rare and that they can be identified by the combination of hsp65 and rpoB typing methods.
6 M. abscessussmooth strains of 2 distinct genotypes with an identical rpoB gene were identified from Korean patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phylogenetic analysis of M. massilience strains with rpoB gene lateral transfer from M. absessus.
the phylogenetic analysis of the M. abscess complex strains that have the recombinant rposB gene.
the first report of Rec-mas strains in Korea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rpoB typing method should be used with caution in identifying M. massiliensis strains.
rpoB typing is not suitable for the discrimination of M. massilience from M. absccessus.
the 6 Rec- mas strains were not M. abscesus but M. massiliensis with a specific rpoB gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rpoB gene is a good candidate for a marker for the phylogenetic analysis of the M. abscessuss complex.
Rec-mas strains may have a specific genetic lineage that is distinct from other M. massiliensetype strains.
the rpoB LGTs in the M. massilense complex may be more frequent than previously expected, and that the rpo B typing may not be a good marker for M. massiliensetype II.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Rec-mas strains are not a new M. abscesssus complex species.
the rpoB sequence analysis may be useful in identifying M. massiliens strains with a specific rpoB gene.
rpoB gene based typing is not a reliable method for the identification of M. massilienese strains.
